BiblicalUsage: The altar is where Israel meets God — earth or stone, built where He puts His name, with fire that never goes out. Noah and Abraham build them on the road, Moses builds one of acacia wood for the tabernacle, and Elijah repairs the broken one on Carmel before he calls down fire.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the altar is the heart of the whole old covenant: God comes down to a place, and sin is dealt with there, by blood, before anyone draws near. That is why the altar never stands empty for long.
RelatedEvents: The Binding of Isaac; The Tabernacle Is Built; Elijah on Mount Carmel
